Mapping optima and the orchestra manifest

Source: vignettes/mapping-optima.Rmd
mapping-optima.Rmd
library(optimix)

Why

A breeder ranking candidate sowing configurations against a cost function does not always want the single best combination back. If several configurations score within noise of each other, the one to actually plant can depend on constraints the cost function never saw – seed availability, rotation history, machinery on hand – and a plain argmin search shows only the first of those configurations it happened to converge to, never the rest. The question this vignette answers is: when a design surface has several solutions of essentially equal merit, can optimix hand back all of them, state plainly when it cannot, and package the answer for a system downstream rather than a person reading a console?

What

optimix_map() returns the distinct optima of a function over a box, rather than a single best point. It has a native path (always available, local search from many starts, clustered) and a premium path (a calibrated Gaussian-mixture map, when a new-enough proxymix is installed), and reports which one ran in its source field. The same intent reaches the main verb through goal = "map" on optimix(): auto then routes to a map-emitting engine, or declines and says so plainly when none fits, marking the returned optimix_result with the optimix_map_abstention class so a caller can detect the decline without parsing prose. as_orchestra_manifest() re-expresses any result – mapped or not – as an orchestra_manifest, the federation’s shared, hashed, typed hand-off object (contract C2 v2 in ORCHESTRA.md’s registry); verify_manifest() checks that hash.

Do

A synthetic surface with four equally good answers

The classic demonstration is a synthetic test surface, Himmelblau’s function, a two-dimensional cost surface with four global minima of equal depth:

himmelblau <- function(x) {
  (x[1]^2 + x[2] - 11)^2 + (x[1] + x[2]^2 - 7)^2
}

Two paths, one function

optimix_map() has a native path and a premium path, and picks between them automatically. The native path is always available: it runs a local search from many Latin-hypercube starts and clusters the converged points into distinct optima, using nothing beyond base R. When a new-enough proxymix is installed, the premium path returns a calibrated Gaussian-mixture map over the optima instead – a queryable posterior, carried in the result’s map field. The result’s source field reports which path produced it:

set.seed(11)
map <- optimix_map(himmelblau, lower = c(-6, -6), upper = c(6, 6))
map
#> <optimix_map> 4 optima found (proxymix)
#>   [1] value 0.214897 at -3.719, -3.240
#>   [2] value 0.325735 at -2.704,  3.137
#>   [3] value 0.347378 at  3.505, -1.783
#>   [4] value 0.451811 at 2.878, 2.049
map$source
#> [1] "proxymix"
Every optimum optimix_map() recovered (source: proxymix).
rank x1 x2 value
1 -3.7192 -3.2403 0.2149
2 -2.7035 3.1372 0.3257
3 3.5050 -1.7831 0.3474
4 2.8781 2.0490 0.4518 
gx <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 120L)
gy <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 120L)
grid_df <- expand.grid(x1 = gx, x2 = gy)
grid_df$z <- apply(
  grid_df, 1L, function(row) himmelblau(c(row[["x1"]], row[["x2"]]))
)
grid_df$z <- pmin(grid_df$z, 500)
modes_df <- data.frame(
  x1 = map$modes[, 1L], x2 = map$modes[, 2L], rank = seq_len(map$n)
)
ggplot2::ggplot(grid_df, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2, z = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_contour_filled(bins = 14L) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "objective\n(capped at 500)",
                                guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = modes_df, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "white", fill = "firebrick", shape = 21L, size = 3L, stroke = 1L
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "x1", y = "x2",
    title = "Himmelblau's synthetic surface: every recovered optimum"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::coord_equal()

Himmelblau’s synthetic function, capped at 500 to keep the four wells legible; the points found by optimix_map() are marked in red, best (deepest) first. Four sit in visually identical, fully dark wells; a fifth, shallower point, when the premium path finds one, is set apart by sitting in a lighter band – exactly the shallow-artefact distinction a single printed value cannot show.

The marked points confirm that optimix_map() returned a genuine set of distinct optima rather than the same well found repeatedly – the outcome a plain argmin search cannot show, since it stops at the first optimum it converges to.

The two paths answer the same question in different registers. On the native path each optimum is polished by a local search, so the printed values sit at effectively zero and the locations are sharp. On the proxymix path the modes are peaks of a fitted mixture – a summary of where the low-value mass lies – so locations are approximate and a shallow extra mode can appear beside the true wells. The modes are printed best first in either case, so deep optima separate from shallow artefacts at a glance, and the modes and values fields give the full set programmatically.

Asking auto for a map

The same intent can be declared on the main verb. goal = "map" steers method = "auto" towards a map-emitting engine, and the result carries the queryable mixture in $map:

set.seed(12)
res <- optimix(himmelblau, lower = c(-6, -6), upper = c(6, 6), goal = "map")
summary(res)
#> Optimisation result
#>   Chosen optimiser : proxymix_map
#>   Reason           : goal = map: proxymix_map returns the full set of optima + a posterior over the optimum (from_objective study, 2026-06-24)
#>   Best value       : 0.057594583
#>   Best parameters  : -3.75873, -3.24823
#>   Evaluations used : 58793
#>   Converged        : yes
#>   Optima mapped    : 6

The mixture path itself spends many cheap evaluations to map the whole optimum set – res$counts runs well above a single-point search’s budget when proxymix is installed and the chunk above executes – so it suits inexpensive objectives, and the selector reaches it only when a map is asked for.

When the map cannot be honoured

The fallback does not fabricate a map, and it is worth seeing happen rather than taking on trust. proxymix_map is registered for problems of dimension 10 or fewer; a 12-dimensional request for goal = "map" is therefore outside its range whether or not proxymix is installed, so auto cannot honour it and falls back to the single best optimum instead of fabricating a map:

set.seed(7)
res_abstain <- optimix(
  function(x) sum((x - 0.4)^2), lower = rep(-3, 12L), upper = rep(3, 12L),
  goal = "map"
)
class(res_abstain)
#> [1] "optimix_map_abstention" "optimix_result"
inherits(res_abstain, "optimix_map_abstention")
#> [1] TRUE
res_abstain$provenance$engine
#> [1] "gensa"
res_abstain$provenance$why
#> [1] "goal = map requested but no map-emitting engine fits this problem (install 'proxymix' for the posterior over all optima, p <= 10); returning the single best optimum via gensa"

optimix_map_abstention is prepended to the result’s class vector rather than replacing it, so every ordinary optimix_result method still applies, and a caller who only wants to know whether the request was honoured can check inherits(x, "optimix_map_abstention") without parsing the why string. The same prepend-not-replace convention marks a non-converged optimum’s manifest with optimix_manifest_abstention, so both declines are recognisable from the class vector alone.

The orchestra manifest

An optimisation result often feeds a downstream system rather than a person, and as_orchestra_manifest() re-expresses a result as a typed hand-off contract for that purpose – the C2 v2 generic orchestra_manifest in ORCHESTRA.md’s contract registry. The optimum rides in params as a one-row table. The typed summary and metadata carry the engine, the convergence verdict, and the true evaluation count. The uncertainty_available flag records whether the manifest carries a posterior over the optimum (a mixture map) or a bare point estimate, so a consumer never mistakes one for the other. The payload is integrity-hashed at emission, and verify_manifest() recomputes the hash to detect any later modification:

best <- optimix(himmelblau, lower = c(-6, -6), upper = c(6, 6),
                method = "base_optim")
m <- as_orchestra_manifest(best)
m@params
#>   par1 par2        value
#> 1    3    2 7.433159e-13
m@summary$headline
#> [1] "optimum f = 7.43316e-13 via base_optim"
m@metadata$uncertainty_available
#> [1] FALSE
verify_manifest(m)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "data_hash verified"

Here a single-point engine produced the result, so the flag is FALSE and the manifest offers only a point estimate, with no invented uncertainty. Had the proxymix mixture engine run, the flag would be TRUE and the metadata would carry the full solution map alongside the optimum.

Read

Native or premium, optimix_map() recovered 4 optima on this run, reported through the result’s source field as “proxymix”. The table lists every one of them; the figure shows why the count alone is not the full picture – whichever points sit in a genuinely dark well are the deep, essentially tied optima, and any point in a lighter band beside them is a shallow artefact of the fitting procedure rather than a fifth true minimum.

With proxymix installed, asking auto for a map directly reaches proxymix_map and spends 58793 evaluations mapping the whole optimum set, an order of magnitude above a single-point search’s typical budget – the price paid for a posterior over every optimum rather than one point.

The 12-dimensional request makes the fallback concrete rather than descriptive: its class carries optimix_map_abstention, optimix_result, confirming optimix_map_abstention sits first, and its provenance names the engine that actually ran (gensa) and the reason the map itself was declined. The manifest section closes the loop from either path to a downstream consumer: m@summary$headline reads “optimum f = 7.43316e-13 via base_optim”, verify_manifest(m)$ok is TRUE, and metadata$uncertainty_available is FALSE because base_optim produced this particular manifest – a point, correctly labelled as one.

A package-level routing study compared optimix’s engines against proxymix’s from_objective() mapper across seven case-classes on functions with known analytic optima, independent of both packages (comparisons/from_objective/, ORCHESTRA_dev, 2026-06-24); its tally is cited here and not recomputed. optimix won five of the seven classes – every regime with a single best point to find, smooth or multimodal, low-dimensional or high – and proxymix won two: recovering every optimum of a multimodal surface in one fit, and returning a genuine posterior over the optimum set. That is exactly the split this vignette walks: reach for optimix_map() when the deliverable is the whole set with a queryable map, and for plain optimix() when it is the single best point.

Limits

Himmelblau’s function is a synthetic two-dimensional textbook surface with four exactly equal minima; it is chosen because the ground truth is known, not because it resembles a fielded design problem, and nothing here demonstrates how many equally good optima a real cost surface tends to carry. The premium path’s mode locations are read off a fitted mixture, not polished by a further local search, so their precision is lower than the native path’s; this vignette does not quantify that gap numerically; a reader who needs an error bound on a proxymix-reported location should treat it as approximate. The 12-dimensional abstention example is chosen to guarantee the decline deterministically, regardless of whether proxymix is installed; it does not explore the boundary case of a problem just inside the mixture engine’s dimension range, where the map may still degrade gracefully rather than abstain outright.

What to read next

Getting started with optimix covers the two front doors and the result object this vignette builds on. The auto selector and racing covers the rest of the selector’s decision surface – noise, expense, budget – that goal = "map" sits alongside. Combinatorial optimisation and delta evaluation covers the one design space neither mapping nor racing reaches: permutations.

Reproduce

Seed 11 for the map, 12 for the goal = "map" call, 7 for the 12-dimensional abstention example.
